title: DLMF 26.18 Counting Techniques: Let A_{1},A_{2},\ldots,A_{n} be subsets of a set S that are not necessarily disjoint.
summary: DLMF 26.18 Counting Techniques: Let A_{1},A_{2},\ldots,A_{n} be subsets of a set S that are not necessarily disjoint.
body: NIST DLMF section 26.18 (Counting Techniques) says: "Let A_{1},A_{2},\ldots,A_{n} be subsets of a set S that are not necessarily disjoint. Then the number of elements in the set S\setminus(A_{1}\cup A_{2}\cup\cdots\cup A_{n}) is The number of positive integers \leq N that are not divisible by any of the primes p_{1},p_{2},\ldots,p_{n} (§ 27.2(i) ) is With the notation of § 26.15 , the number of placements of n nonattacking rooks on an n\times n chessboard that avoid the squares in a specified subset B is The number of ways of placing n labeled objects into k labeled boxes so that at least one object is in each box is Note that this is also one of the counting problems for which a formula is given in Table 26.17.1 . Elements of N are labeled, elements of K are labeled, and f is onto. For further examples in the use of generating functions, see Stanley ( 1997 , 1999 ) and Wilf ( 1994 ) . See also Pólya et al. ( 1983 ) ." Equation 26.18.1 on the page has alt text "\left|S\setminus(A_{1}\cup A_{2}\cup\cdots\cup A_{n})\right|=\left|S\right|+% \sum_{t=1}^{n}(-1)^{t}\sum_{1\leq j_{1}<j_{2}<\cdots<j_{t}\leq n}\left|A_{j_{1% }}\cap A_{j_{2}}\cap\cdots\cap A_{j_{t}}\right|.". Equation 26.18.2 on the page has alt text "N+\sum_{t=1}^{n}(-1)^{t}\sum_{1\leq j_{1}<j_{2}<\cdots<j_{t}\leq n}\left% \lfloor\frac{N}{p_{j_{1}}p_{j_{2}}\cdots p_{j_{t}}}\right\rfloor.". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
